The account rests on one empirical claim worth checking before anything else: that the disputes track vagueness and change rather than reliability or bad faith. If the reader finds that written, specific agreements are still being broken, the diagnosis is wrong and the process advice will not help, and the problem lies elsewhere.

Taking up the written-agreement proposal commits the reader to specifying what "done" means for each contested chore before assigning it, which requires conceding that standards legitimately differ between the three of them and must actually be negotiated rather than treated as obvious. It also depends on everyone consulting the same record, so a chat or board the avoiding friend never reads fails silently.

The check-in proposal presumes schedules will keep changing, as the reader reports; its value drops if the household stabilizes, and it presumes at least the avoiding friend will accept some meeting format, which is exactly what is in doubt. The default rule that silence leaves the old agreement in force is contestable from the other side as well — it can entrench an arrangement one person never wanted.

The proposal to treat non-response to a written offer as consent is the most vulnerable item: it risks converting withdrawal into agreement and deepening the friend's retreat. Anyone adopting it should expect the fairness objection and be ready to attach an early review date or drop the move entirely.

A criticism the whole approach invites: even the light version imposes ongoing initiation and upkeep on the reader, unpaid coordination labor falling on the person least at fault. That cost is real and may not be sustainable, and nothing here distributes it.

The account assumes the reader's own agreements are not a major source of the vagueness; using it fairly includes auditing one's own habits first.

entries.verbatim: Taking this account up means treating its conjectures as revisable, not established. The ambiguity conjecture stands or falls with a simple test: record the next few agreements in writing with task, owner, definition of done, and deadline; if disputes recur anyway, the conjecture weakens and attention should shift to the differing-standards thread or to accumulated resentment, which this account keeps separate. The proposed actions are a written shared record, a short trial of a rotation or swap-based arrangement with explicit rebalancing rules, a brief recurring check-in, and a one-on-one with the avoiding friend aimed at making the conversations cheaper rather than at any specific chore. These carry stated risks: a visible ledger between friends can produce scorekeeping and may inflame rather than reassure, and whether tracking helps this particular group is left unresolved pending the trial. The advice depends on all three flatmates being willing to try something; if the avoider refuses every format, the problem changes shape — toward whether the living arrangement is viable — and this account does not cover that case. Scope is limited to ordinary chore conflict between friends; if the arguments are carrying a deeper rupture in the friendship, a different account is needed. No prior account was carried into this invocation, since the selected input was absent, so nothing here is inherited; later accounts should revise these conjectures against what the asker reports back rather than extend them by inertia.

entries.verbatim: Taking up this objection means treating it as a set of checks on the selected account, not as a rival account with its own package. Its usable claims are that the account should stop assuming the asker stands outside the conflict; that the avoidance explanation be demoted from assertion to hypothesis, with the one-on-one reframed as open diagnosis rather than format negotiation; that the written-agreements trial be described as an intervention whose results underdetermine causes, with the act of proposing a ledger counted among its risks; that decoupling options such as own zones, separate supplies, or paid cleaning enter the solution space alongside rotations; and that past fairness grievances receive their own lever instead of being folded into future allocation. What this objection does not claim: it does not dispute the standards-versus-division distinction or the rotation-over-fixed-rota point, both of which are explicitly carried over, and it leaves standing the account's stated limits, including its scope restriction to ordinary chore conflict and its dependence on three willing participants. Weaknesses of the objection itself: its readings of the arguing and the avoidance rest on a thin problem statement and could be wrong in either direction; the claim that proposing a ledger signals distrust is a conjecture about social meaning, not an observation; decoupling may be ruled out by money or the flat's layout; and the intervention-versus-measurement point applies equally to any trial this objection would motivate, so it counsels modest claims about evidence rather than abandonment of trials. No prior accounts were consulted and none are inherited. If a later account revises the selected one along these lines, the revision should still be tested against what the asker reports next rather than adopted wholesale.

entries.verbatim:
The load-bearing claims here are conjectures, and taking this up means treating them as such. The claim that avoidance signals coordination overload rather than conflict-aversion or disengagement is testable in principle — by counting how many distinct agreements the household is maintaining, shrinking that count, and watching whether avoidance and re-litigation fall — but the test is confounded, since any shrink also changes what people argue about, and a drop in disputes could reflect fewer occasions rather than less friction. The claim that rotas and swap rules generate renegotiation load beyond what schedule churn explains is reasoning, not observation; nothing in the exposed material shows whether these flatmates actually renegotiate often or simply fail to comply.

The cleaner proposal carries explicit dependences: money from all three, willingness to spend it on this, and enough residual goodwill to organize the hire — which is itself a conversation, the scarce resource. If that conversation cannot be had, the buyout is moot. The 'ask before proposing' step depends on the avoider answering even a low-stakes question; silence there does not distinguish overload from withdrawal from the friendship, and the two call for different responses.

A live criticism of the whole framing: privatization is easy for dishes and impossible for the hallway floor, so some irreducible commons remains, and shrinking may simply concentrate resentment on the lowest-threshold flatmate, who ends up owning the residual by default. A second criticism: reducing the shared surface could confirm distance rather than relieve it, if any of the three experiences joint chores as part of what makes this a friendship rather than a tenancy arrangement. Both criticisms stand against the rival as posed and are not answered here.

Unresolved: if both flatmates answer 'no problem worth a system' while chores still go undone, the asker faces a choice the framing does not resolve — accept the resulti
